messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started for release v1.42.3 -> eu-canary (slot eu-canary-12). batch=50, target=200 :rocket:

sre_lead: seeing a sharp tail-latency spike and a few 5xxs in EU ingress. looks correlated with redis failovers :eyes:

ops-oncall: opened incident #INC-2024-457 (eu-redis). redis nodes flapping, failover churn ongoing. ETA for stabilization unknown

release_manager: holding all EU-facing releases. @deploy-bot pause canaries and pin active version for safety. we do NOT want partial rollout during redis instability :no_entry_sign:

andrew: agree — abort the canary and pin to last known-good (v1.41.8). we can re-run canary once incident cleared and perf stable.

maria: quick note for release notes: mark v1.42.3 as "suspended due to infra incident", will follow up with timeline. I'll draft customer comms if we end up delaying >4h :writing_hand:

deploy-bot: Action: pause_canary executed by release_manager at 6790012352. Canary state: ABORTED -> ROLLBACK_PENDING. Pin applied: target_version=v1.41.8 (sticky)

product_pm: who will own rollback if needed? can we avoid full rollback by aborting canary only?

andrew: aborting only should be enough because canary nodes didn't fully roll forward. rollback is a safety path if we observe persisted errors after commit.

sre_lead: current plan: stabilize redis cluster -> run short soak (30m) against staging EU -> smoke test traffic -> then greenlight new canary. if redis cycles again we keep rollouts blocked.

release_manager: proposed reschedule window: 2024-11-02T18:00Z -> 2024-11-02T20:00Z (UTC) for a controlled retry. @ops-oncall + @sre_lead confirm before we unpause.

ops-oncall: +1 on the window but will confirm after incident update. If we still see >1% 5xxs during soak we keep hold.

kate: I'll update the deploy checklist and add an explicit pre-canary redis-health check (script + manual signoff). putting owner in doc: @kate.

deploy-bot: Reschedule created: v1.42.3 -> retry window 2024-11-02T18:00Z-20:00Z. Rollout policy: canary=50->200, auto-abort on >0.5% errors for 10m, pre-check=redis_health=pass.

maria: customer comms draft in #marketing-drafts in 15m. short notice: "We paused a deployment for EU region due to a backend infrastructure incident. No customer data impacted; we'll retry once services are stable."

release_manager: action items:
- @sre_lead: update incident timeline and signal when redis healthy
- @ops-oncall: confirm reschedule window is safe before we unpause
- @kate: add pre-check + test run steps to checklist
- @maria: customer note ready if delay >4h

andrew: tagging follow-up: after unpause run a 30m load soak at canary traffic before scaling to 200. keep verbose tracing enabled for first 10k requests.

deploy-bot: Note: pinned version v1.41.8 will remain in effect for EU until explicit unpin command from release_manager.

sre_lead: incident update at +12m: one redis replica still cycling, but failover rate decreased. will update again in 20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

release_manager: thanks all. keeping thread here for reschedule updates. will only unpin/unpause after explicit "cleared" from @sre_lead and ops signoff. :white_check_mark:
